title: Geometric Phonon Energy Pumping in a Layer-Hybridized Moiré Exciton Manifold
authors: Bitap Raj Thakuria, Himangshu Prabal Goswami
abstract: Slow cyclic modulation of an open quantum system can generate a geometric contribution to its energy transfer statistics, separable from the dynamic background. In this work we construct an experimentally anchored four state open system model for a gate-tunable WSe2/WS2 moiré exciton manifold within a population level full counting statistics framework. We first drive the system uniformly through a closed gate and pump loop and separate the geometric contribution from the dynamic background by reversing the loop direction. We then examine how this response changes with environmental rates, exciton coupling, control conditions, and static spectral broadening. A shorter cycle period followed by nonuniform traversal of the driving loop substantially improves detectability while preserving the geometric response. Combined with enhanced phonon relaxation and reduced radiative loss, this gives about a fourteenfold fixed time signal to noise gain relative to the uniform loop. Our results show that the geometric phonon response remains robust against realistic variations in the system and its environment, and that we can improve its detectability more effectively by suppressing dynamical noise through frequency modulated driving.
summary: The research develops a method to extract a purely geometric component of energy pumping from an exciton manifold by analyzing its energy transfer statistics via Full Counting Statistics. By implementing optimized, non-uniform driving protocols, the authors demonstrate a significant enhancement in signal detectability while proving the robustness of this geometric signature against realistic environmental noise.
main_problem: The work aims to generate and detect a geometric contribution to energy transfer statistics (geometric phonon pumping) from slow cyclic modulation in an open quantum system, separating it from dynamic noise.
main_result: A Non-Uniform Field Modulation (NUFM) driving protocol significantly enhances the signal-to-noise ratio by suppressing dynamical fluctuations while robustly retaining the geometric pumping signal across realistic environmental variations.
method: The analysis employs Full Counting Statistics (FCS) applied to a master equation framework, separating energy cumulants into dynamic and geometric parts based on loop traversal direction reversal.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as a gate-tunable WSe2/WS2 moiré exciton manifold, treated as an open quantum system governed by a Liouvillian approach. The dynamics are analyzed using concepts derived from the tilted master equation and adiabatic approximations.
key_observables: Geometric first cumulant ($C_{	ext{geo},1}$), dynamic mean ($	ext{Cdyn}_1$), cycle-to-cycle fluctuation ($C_2$), and the fixed-time intrinsic Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR).
important_parameters: Gate voltage modulation rate, pump intensity modulation rate, environmental relaxation rates (phonon/radiative loss), and the cycle period ($	au$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the adiabatic approximation for slow driving and models coupling to the environment via phenomenological rate terms rather than fully coherent Hamiltonian terms.
figures_summary: Figures compare performance metrics (like SNR) between uniform vs. NUFM traversals, show period dependence of signal retention, and illustrate the local mechanism involving relaxation gaps and control parameter rates.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework using FCS for open systems, develops the geometric separation technique via loop reversal, optimizes the driving protocol by comparing uniform versus non-uniform modulation (NUFM), and finally validates the robustness of the enhanced signal against varying physical parameters.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, measurable signature—the geometric contribution to energy transfer statistics—in a solid-state platform. The methodology for separating this topological/geometric feature from thermal noise using advanced counting statistics is highly relevant to open quantum system dynamics in condensed matter.
